Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness band similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. I've been using WHOOP for six months and honestly think this is the right direction, but I hope Apple can do better in a few areas.

Since the product is still in the early stages of development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screenless fitness band, and it may not launch until 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a thin fabric band with built-in sensors and a computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer discounts or free WHOOP devices for Sapphire credit card holders—I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around that time, but I haven't been able to use it consistently with full commitment.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never 100% accurate, and I find it too much of a hassle to specifically take out my phone to log a workout—whether before or after. Apple Watch can start tracking directly from the watch face, while WHOOP can sync timing through Apple Health. This is also the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm working out at the gym, taking out my phone is acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or strolling for a bit, I don't want to specifically take out my phone to record the activity.

So for Apple's screenless fitness band, I sincerely hope they can include a combination of buttons and indicator lights that allow users to start and stop workout tracking. The categorization of activity types would still need to be handled later on the phone, but I'd rather do that after the workout than fiddle with it during the workout. Apple could also develop classification models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple manages to create a screenless fitness band that is easy to use and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This design has several advantages, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Personally, after using WHOOP, I still lean towards wearing a smartwatch, even if it comes at the cost of battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's "Do Not Disturb mode" solves this problem.

What are your thoughts on Apple developing a screenless fitness band? How much would you be willing to pay for one? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
